liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): The China Cat intro is described as extremely crisp and precise; The jam linking China Cat to Rider contains a short passage that sounds like UJB [8][10]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Reviewer found this Rider wonderful, evoking blue skies, high clouds and northern Arizona [10]
- **Eyes of the World** (1 review): Reviewer ranks this Eyes among the tightest ever played, comparing it with other versions [8]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Sugar Magnolia is called incendiary by the reviewer [16]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Saturday Night is called incendiary, with raw power-chord rock playing [16]

## Setlist highlights

- **Filer - Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [17]
- **GoinÃÂ Down The Road FeelinÃÂ Bad**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd73-11-25.sbd.sacks.2213.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 25 songs; 201 min; rated 4.61/5 by 18 [1]. Said about its sound: Vocals sound unusually clear and full for 1973, without the thin, tinny quality common to recordings from that year; Reviewer finds the soundboard's sound close to perfect throughout; Reviewer says this sounds outstanding [7][8][15]
- **gd1973-11-25.150897.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd1973-11-25.150853.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 22 songs; 175 min [4]
- **gd1973-11-25.sbd.miller.113007.flac16**: soundboard; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 4.75/5 by 16 [2]

## Around the show

- Promoter Barry Fey printed Feyline Field on tickets; the show was actually held at Tempe's Diablo Stadium, a minor league ballpark [11]
- The small outdoor ballpark was overwhelmed by the size of the sound system [11]
- Reviewer was a 15-year-old backstage; a friend from Guadalajara photographed from the stage, and the day was cold [14]
- In the last half of the final set, Jerry plays fewer solos and more basic power chords, with Donna in the mix [16]
- Barry Fey had bought the old Tempe Diablo stadium and staged a series of shows there, including Allman Brothers, Leon Russell and Traffic [19]
- This show closed out the west coast leg of the Dead's fall tour [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd73-11-25.sbd.sacks.2213.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Filler tracks in the middle of the tape (Me and My Uncle, The Other One, Mexicali Blues, Wharf Rat) come from the Felt Forum show of 1971-12-04; Five filler tracks sit in the middle of the show on this tape, and the reviewer removed them; Credits Darrin Sacks with a great transfer of this soundboard [1][9][12][15]
- **gd1973-11-25.150897.sbd.patched.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 13, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master > Dat (44.1k) [3]. Also: Soundboard to cassette master to reel, then another reel via Panasonic RS1506, then Tascam DA-3000 at DSF 1-bit/5.6MHz; This patched version fills gaps in Playing in the Band and Let It Grow, using patch source from Matt Smith [3]
- **gd1973-11-25.150853.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 8, 2020; source: SBD > Reel Master > Dat (44.1k) [4]. Also: Upgrade to the uploader's earlier transfer, with pitch correction settings supplied by Joe B. Jones [4]
- **gd1973-11-25.sbd.miller.113007.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Dat [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Feyline Field - November 25, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/november-25-1973) [23]
